date_note: Date of Yamato's notice; the page gives no earlier public day. The notice says the third-party access to the vendor's servers was on 13 November.
title: Yamato Holdings says customer data may have leaked after unauthorized access to its chat vendor's servers
summary: Yamato Holdings' notice of 25 November says Chatplus Inc., which provides the chat service Yamato uses for customer inquiries, reported that a third party accessed some of its servers on 13 November. For the foreign-language chat, customers' names, addresses and phone numbers may have leaked; Yamato says card information and passwords are not included. The notice gives no number of affected customers.
plain: Yamato says a third party accessed servers of its chat vendor Chatplus. Names, addresses and phone numbers of foreign-language chat users may have leaked; Yamato says no card data or passwords are involved.
exec: Yamato says a vendor's chat servers were accessed and some customer contact details may have leaked; it gave no number of customers.
action: Yamato asks customers to use the inquiry form or phone while chat is suspended, to be alert to fake emails, SMS or calls impersonating Yamato, and not to open URLs or attachments in unexpected messages.

validation.note: Yamato's own notice read; the Cybersecurity.com (Japan) article relays it.

review.note: Compared title, date, 13 Nov access, data fields, no-number, action with Yamato notice and Cybersecurity.com
